title: Leo's $6,000 Card Will Cost Him $12,000

scenes.say: Leo owes $6,000 on a credit card. He pays $150, every single month.
Sounds responsible. But his card charges about 24% a year.
That's roughly $120 of interest, every month.
So out of his $150, only about $30 touches the debt.
At that pace, it takes almost 7 years to pay off.
He'd pay about $12,200 in total. Half of it is pure interest.
Now watch what $300 a month does.
Debt free in about 26 months, and interest drops to roughly $1,700.
The extra $150? Pause one subscription, cook two more dinners a week, sell one thing.
Same card, and he keeps about $4,500 in his pocket.
What's the APR on your card? Check it, before you pay $150 a month for 7 years.

visual.text: What's the APR on your card?

question: What's the APR on your card? Most people have to look it up.
description: Leo owes about $6,000 on a card at roughly 24% APR and pays $150 a month. Here's why that takes almost 7 years and about $12,200 — and how doubling the payment cuts it to about 26 months and saves roughly $4,500 in interest. Estimates assume a fixed 24% APR and no new charges.
